contract: DELETE /api/custom-metadata-providers/:id is admin-only (401 without a token, 403 for a normal user, admin check before the id lookup; 404 for an unknown id as admin). For a stored id it answers 200, deletes the row, sets every library whose provider is custom-<id> back to google (book mediaType) or itunes (podcast) and emits custom_metadata_provider_removed. A second delete is 404. A later search with the removed slug answers 200 with an empty array.
exceptions: force is not applicable: the delete route has no force/hard mode; a destructive delete is the only behaviour.
The removed provider's previously fetched covers are not re-derived: the route updates the provider column only, and no library metadata is rewritten.

invariants.contract: DELETE /api/custom-metadata-providers/:id as the admin answers 200, removes the row and its list entry, leaves the other providers, and a following book search with that slug answers 200 with an empty array; deleting the same id again answers 404 with the rows unchanged. No response body is contracted: the web client branches on the status only.

Deleting a book provider used as a library's provider sets that library's provider column to google, and deleting a podcast provider sets its library back to itunes, without changing either library's name or mediaType.
Deleting the last custom podcast provider answers 200, removes it from the admin list, leaves GET /api/search/providers podcasts as only itunes and books with the remaining custom book provider.

DELETE /api/custom-metadata-providers/:id answers 401 without a token, 403 for a non-admin for an existing and an unknown id (the admin check precedes the lookup) and 404 for an unknown id as admin, and a rejected delete removes no row.
